source: the game manual, read rather than recalled: Contra (Re-Translation).pdf in archive.org/details/rx2MRPnes1250pxPDF — the Japanese Famicom manual, which is the one matching this ROM. See docs/manuals.md. Entries below name the page they come from.
notes: The wall at the end of the jungle is destroyed by its cannons and the sensor between them; point-blank diagonal fire is what reaches them.
A base stage does not scroll. Its exit opens when the room's sensor is destroyed, and the way on is upward through the door.
Flying capsules carry weapons; shooting one and walking into what it drops is worth a detour.
Once a room's sensor is destroyed the way on is upward through the door, so a cleared room rewards moving up the screen.
The door out of a base room is in the middle of the far wall, near screen x=112; walking up anywhere else does nothing.

scope.why: the base: byte 48 is the stage counter and 1 is the base. The manual says these things about a base stage — it does not scroll, its exit opens when the sensor dies, and the way on is upward. Applied to the jungle they tell the planner to climb and stand firing.
scope.target_px_why: the base: a room sensor is 8 hit points and destroying it opens the room, worth 667 px by the stage arithmetic (4000 over the six rooms measured 15 September). 667/8 = 83 px per hit point.
scope.target_types_why: the base: the manual says Base 1 is a maze where you destroy sensors and avoid the Royal Guard, so only the sensor is a target here. The rooms do carry wall-typed objects — 44 hit points of type 17 in room 3, 22 in rooms 1 and 4 — and counting those as targets priced a room at several times what it is worth.

target_px_why: scrolling stages: the wall at the end of a zone is 72 hit points (WALL_HP0, from the scan) and destroying it ends the stage, which is worth the distance left to the 4000 stride — about 928 px from the wall at 3072. 928/72 = 13 px per hit point. The old 40 was picked by hand and swamped progress: a whole screen is 256 px.
